headline: High: Aci can trigger broad network egress into Kestra workflows, creating dangerous data leakage and cascading action risk by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest external content through MCP/function calls and Kestra can read/write files and run workflows, so a shared file or workflow handoff could carry attacker-controlled instructions. This is not proven by direct pair evidence, but both profiles expose a plausible bridge. The risk is lower than high because no default shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF Aci writes untrusted content into a file or workflow input that Kestra later parses as instructions
IF Kestra is configured to consume Aci outputs from a shared workspace or stdin/stdout bridge
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff directory with strict file naming
Strip instruction-like text from Aci outputs before passing to Kestra
Require a human review step before Kestra executes Aci-produced artifacts
Disable shared filesystem handoff unless needed
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all Aci-to-Kestra payloads

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; Kestra can read files, write files, and call many external APIs. If they share a workspace or workflow payloads, sensitive records can flow from Aci into Kestra and then out to third-party services. The pairwise path is plausible in default enterprise setups, so severity is high.
conditions: IF Aci outputs CRM/email/calendar data into a shared file or workflow artifact
IF Kestra forwards that artifact to Slack, email, cloud storage, or another API
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive test data
Disable outbound connectors in Kestra for Aci-fed workflows
Mask email, CRM, and calendar fields before handoff
Review Kestra task definitions for external sinks
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists per workflow

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and broad API calls, while Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and elevated privileges. Both can mutate shared resources and external systems, so concurrent runs can overwrite files, duplicate actions, or race on the same APIs. The overlap is broad enough that default coordination is unsafe.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path, API account, or workflow state
IF Kestra runs Aci-triggered jobs concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts per agent
Use per-run unique output directories
Serialize writes to shared resources
Disable concurrent execution for shared targets
requires-engineering: add distributed locks around mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Kestra can execute workflows, shell commands, and external API calls. If Kestra treats Aci output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated Aci result can cascade into automated downstream actions with real-world impact. No verification mechanism is documented in either profile, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Aci output as a trigger or task parameter without validation
IF the resulting workflow sends messages, updates records, or runs shell commands
mitigations: Insert a validation step before any Kestra action
Require human approval for high-impact tasks
Log and diff Aci outputs before execution
Limit Aci outputs to suggestions, not commands
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all Aci-to-Kestra inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, while Kestra processes logs, artifacts, database data, and cloud storage data. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, but the shared data classes create a realistic compliance mismatch risk if Aci-fed data is retained or routed differently by Kestra. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Aci data is stored in Kestra logs or artifacts beyond the source system's retention policy
IF EU or regulated records are routed through Kestra connectors without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields in workflow inputs
Set short retention on Kestra logs and artifacts
Document data residency for each connector
Review whether regulated data enters either system
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency policy enforcement
